content: 1. Aluminum hydroxide and azithromycin: Aluminum hydroxide reduces azithromycin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. To minimize this effect, separate their administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 2. Aluminum hydroxide and baloxavir marboxil: Aluminum hydroxide decreases baloxavir levels due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction is significant, and alternative therapies should be considered. Studies in monkeys have shown that concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly reduces plasma levels. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 3. Magnesium hydroxide and baloxavir marboxil: Magnesium hydroxide also reduces baloxavir levels through cation binding. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate doses by at least 2 hours. 4. Aluminum hydroxide and benazepril: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the effects of benazepril, likely by reducing its absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider separating doses by 2 hours. 5. Aluminum hydroxide and beta-blockers (e.g., bisoprolol, betaxolol, carvedilol): Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of these beta-blockers by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 6. Aluminum hydroxide and cefdinir, cefditoren, cefpodoxime, cefuroxime: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of these cephalosporins by increasing gastric pH, which affects their absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate doses by at least 2 hours. 7. Aluminum hydroxide and ciprofloxacin: Aluminum hydroxide significantly reduces ciprofloxacin levels by up to 90% due to cation binding. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide. 8. Aluminum hydroxide and ketoconazole/itraconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of these antifungal agents by increasing gastric pH, which reduces their solubility and absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, administer the antifungal at least 2 hours before or after aluminum hydroxide. 9. Aluminum hydroxide and iron supplements (e.g., ferrous fumarate, ferrous sulfate): Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of iron supplements by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate doses by at least 2 hours. 10. Magnesium hydroxide and tetracyclines (e.g., doxycycline, demeclocycline): Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of tetracyclines by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, separate doses by at least 2 hours. 11. Aluminum hydroxide and gabapentin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases gabapentin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 12. Aluminum hydroxide and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: Aluminum hydroxide reduces ledipasvir levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility. Separate administration by at least 4 hours and monitor closely. 13. Magnesium hydroxide and fluoroquinolones (e.g., levofloxacin, gemifloxacin): Magnesium hydroxide reduces the levels of these antibiotics by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, separate doses by at least 2 hours. 14. Aluminum hydroxide and digoxin: Aluminum hydroxide increases digoxin levels by altering gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider alternative therapies if necessary. 15. Aluminum hydroxide and isoniazid: Aluminum hydroxide reduces isoniazid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 16. Magnesium hydroxide and dolutegravir: Magnesium hydroxide reduces dolutegravir levels through cation binding. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium hydroxide. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Aluminum hydroxide and erythromycin: Aluminum hydroxide increases erythromycin levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Aluminum hydroxide and lanthanum carbonate: Aluminum hydroxide interacts with lanthanum carbonate through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer aluminum hydroxide at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum carbonate. 19. Aluminum hydroxide and antiretrovirals (e.g., bictegravir, elvitegravir): Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of these drugs through cation binding. Administer the antiretroviral at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after aluminum hydroxide. Monitor closely and consider alternative therapies if necessary. 20. Aluminum hydroxide and proton pump inhibitors (PPIs): Aluminum hydroxide may reduce the solubility and absorption of drugs that require an acidic environment, such as PPIs. Use caution, monitor closely, and separate doses by at least 2 hours. This summary highlights the key interactions and recommendations for managing them. Always consult a healthcare professional for specific guidance.
